axis: plainly naming the faculty of judging → praising it as fine, sound or tactful

members.tone: Lofty praise - credits a penetrating grasp of how things stand in relation, where *judgment* only names the faculty.
The same commendation built plainly off the adjective, heavier in the mouth than *sagacity* and less polished for it.
The flat name for the ability to tell relations apart, stating the capacity without the admiration *sagacity* loads onto it.
The British spelling of the same neutral faculty-name, adding nothing to *judgment* but a letter.
Praise pitched at fineness - the stress falls on discriminating what a coarser mind would run together.
Compact and admiring, with 'good' built into the word, and it covers seeing with the eyes or the figurative equivalent alike.
Approving at the workaday end - soundness in practical matters, the kind expected of anyone rather than marvelled at.
The bare commendation, with 'good' carrying the whole judgement and no claim past soundness.
Informal and hearty - the same practical soundness spoken of as a homely possession rather than an intellectual one.
Informal and blunt, naming what *common sense* names with a grin at its own plainness.
The barest member - practical soundness in one syllable, with nothing qualifying it.
Homely and affectionate where *good sense* is flatly commendatory, though the soundness praised is the same.
Formal praise for judgment that comes out well, not merely for having the faculty at all.
Praise for a tactful kind of knowing - steering clear of what would embarrass or distress before it arises.
The same avoidance named off the adjective, drier and more clinical than *discretion*.
Tilts the same skill toward wariness - looking all round a situation for the embarrassment or distress in it.
